title: Everyday Technology Words
summary: Learn four common technology words we use every day. Practice how to talk about your phone, apps, charger, and password.

sections.p: A phone is a device we use to call friends and send messages. An app is a small program on your phone. You can use apps to play games, listen to music, or take photos. We use phones and apps every single day to stay connected.

ex.en: I need to buy a new phone.
ex.mean: I want to get a different telephone.
Please put this program on your phone.

sections.p: A charger is a cable or device that gives power to your phone. When your phone battery is low, you need a charger to make it work again. You plug it into the wall and into your phone.

ex.en: My phone battery is dead. Where is my charger?
ex.mean: My phone has no power. I need the cable to charge it.

ex.en: Do you have an iPhone charger?
ex.mean: Can I borrow a cable for my Apple phone?

sections.p: A password is a secret word or numbers. You use a password to open your phone or log into an app. It keeps your personal information safe from other people so they cannot see your messages.

ex.en: Type your password to unlock the screen.
ex.mean: Put in your secret word to see your phone.
I cannot remember my secret numbers.

tip: Write your tech words on sticky notes and put them on your actual phone or computer charger to remember them faster!

quiz.en: I use my ___ to call my mother every Sunday.
My battery is at 2%. Where is my ___?
You need to type your ___ to open this secure app.
I want to download a new fitness ___ to count my steps.
Keep your ___ a secret so no one can open your device.
This small ___ helps me edit my photos easily.
